    Fetch works from OpenAlex

    Source: R/fetch-openalex.R
    sm_fetch_openalex.Rd

    Query the OpenAlex API for scholarly works and return the results as an sm_corpus.

    Supports both free-text search (query) and structured filter syntax (filter). Uses cursor-based pagination to retrieve up to n_max works. Set an OpenAlex API key (see "API key and rate limits").

    Besides cited_by_count, the works keep OpenAlex's field-weighted citation impact (fwci), its citation percentile (citation_percentile, 0 to 1, with the flags is_top_10pct and is_top_1pct) and the date of these values (citations_as_of), and the corpus gets the yearly citation counts as citations_by_year (see sm_corpus() and sm_citation_window()). The openalexR engine has no percentile, so its three percentile columns are NA. To add these fields to a corpus from another source, use sm_enrich_openalex_impact().

    Usage

    sm_fetch_openalex(
  query = NULL,
  filter = NULL,
  n_max = 200L,
  per_page = 200L,
  mailto = Sys.getenv("SCIMAPR_MAILTO"),
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OPENALEX_API_KEY"),
  engine = c("native", "openalexR", "auto"),
  batch_size = 50L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

    Arguments

    query

    Free-text search query passed to the search parameter. If NULL, filter must be supplied.

    filter

    A character string using OpenAlex filter syntax, e.g. "from_publication_date:2020-01-01,type:journal-article".

    n_max

    Maximum number of works to return (default 200).

    per_page

    Number of results per page (max 200).

    mailto

    Contact address sent with each request as the mailto parameter. Read from the SCIMAPR_MAILTO environment variable by default. OpenAlex no longer gives such requests a larger budget (the API key does), and the openalexR engine does not send it.

    api_key

    OpenAlex API key. Read from the OPENALEX_API_KEY environment variable by default; see "API key and rate limits".

    engine

    One of "native" (built-in httr2 client), "openalexR" (use the openalexR package), or "auto" (use openalexR if version 3.1.1 or later is installed, otherwise native).

    batch_size

    Integer; maximum number of |-joined values allowed in a single OpenAlex filter clause before the request is automatically split into multiple batched requests. OpenAlex limits the number of values in an OR filter and the overall URL length, so long DOI (or other ID) lists are chunked, fetched per batch, and row-bound with de-duplication. Default 50, which stays comfortably under the API's documented limit of 100.

    verbose

    Print progress messages?

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    An sm_corpus object. Its provenance records the search (query, filter, n_max and engine), so that sm_rebuild_from_cert() can run it again.

    API key and rate limits

    OpenAlex expects a free API key. Requests without one share one small daily budget with everyone on the same network address; once it is used up, OpenAlex answers HTTP 429 (too many requests) until the budget resets at midnight UTC. Set the key in the OPENALEX_API_KEY environment variable (for example in ~/.Renviron) or pass it as api_key. It is sent in the Authorization header, never in the URL, and it is stored nowhere in the corpus.

    On HTTP 429 the function stops at once with an error of class scimapR_openalex_rate_limit instead of waiting: the message gives the reset time and the remaining budget that OpenAlex reports (the fields reset_at and remaining of the condition) and says whether a key was sent. Only a wait of up to two seconds (OpenAlex also limits requests per second) is waited out, once. Other failed requests stop with class scimapR_openalex_failed; both classes inherit from scimapR_openalex_error. With engine = "openalexR" the openalexR package (version 3.1.1 or later) sends the requests: it gets the key too and its own retries are switched off, but it does not pass on the response headers, so the reset time and the budget are not known.

    Failed requests

    Native requests retry transient server and network failures, and short announced rate-limit waits. Long waits abort immediately. If a later page fails, the error inherits from scimapR_fetch_incomplete and holds the earlier parsed works in rlang::last_error()$partial. Their metadata records fetch_incomplete with the source, received and expected counts, and failure reason. If those pages cannot be parsed, partial is NULL. The default remains an error; an incomplete fetch is never returned as an ordinary successful result.

    See also

    sm_enrich_openalex_impact(), sm_citation_window()

    Other fetchers: sm_fetch_arxiv(), sm_fetch_biorxiv(), sm_fetch_crossref(), sm_fetch_orcid(), sm_fetch_overton(), sm_fetch_pubmed(), sm_fetch_semantic_scholar()

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
corpus <- sm_fetch_openalex(query = "bibliometrics", n_max = 10)
print(corpus)
} # }
